claim: General elections are held in November of even-numbered years
quote: A general election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November in each even-numbered year.

claim: The primary is held in May of every general election year
quote: A primary election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May of each year in which a general election is held.

claim: County officers, county commissioners, county council, township trustee and township board are elected at the general election every four years
quote: shall be elected at the general election before their terms of office expire and every four (4) years thereafter

claim: The offices elected at the general election include county assessor, commissioners, council, township trustee and township board
quote: (8) County assessor. (9) County commissioner. (10) County council member. (11) Township trustee. (12) Township board member.

claim: Municipal elections are held in November every four years in the odd-numbered year before a presidential election (2027, 2031 and so on)
quote: a municipal election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November 2023, 2027, 2031

claim: Municipal primaries are held in May of the same odd-numbered years
quote: a municipal primary election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in May 2023, 2027, 2031

claim: The odd-year municipal schedule covers all cities, towns of 3,500 or more, and every town in Marion County
quote: Towns having a population of three thousand five hundred (3,500) or more.

claim: Towns in a county with a consolidated city follow that schedule regardless of population
quote: Towns located entirely or partially within a county having a consolidated city, regardless of their population.

claim: A town may adopt an ordinance to stagger council terms
quote: a town may adopt an ordinance during the year preceding a municipal election conducted under section 2 of this chapter prescribing the length of the term of office for town legislative body members

claim: Towns with staggered council terms, or an ordinance moving their elections, vote alongside a general election
quote: shall conduct a municipal election in that town that coincides with a general election

claim: A town under 3,500 outside Marion County may move its elections to general election years by ordinance
quote: That the elections for town offices shall be held during general elections or municipal elections, or both.

claim: A town election may not be held in the year after a presidential election
quote: A town election may not be held in a year following a year in which an election for presidential electors is held.

claim: An ordinance moving town elections cannot be repealed for twelve years
quote: The ordinance may not be repealed earlier than twelve (12) years after the ordinance was adopted.

claim: A town over 10,000 may adopt a seven-member council elected in two different years
quote: Four (4) members of the legislative body are elected during a year that municipal elections are held

claim: Home rule applies to every county, municipality and township
quote: "Unit" means county, municipality, or township.

claim: Home rule gives units all powers needed for local affairs, even if not granted by statute
quote: all other powers necessary or desirable in the conduct of its affairs, even though not granted by statute

claim: Home rule does not reach elections: a unit has no power to legislate on or conduct an election unless a statute expressly grants it
quote: or otherwise conduct an election, except as expressly granted by statute

claim: A voter may vote in a party primary if they voted for most of that party's nominees at the last general election, or intend to at the next
quote: at the last general election, voted for a majority of the regular nominees of the political party holding the primary election

claim: A primary voter can be challenged on party affiliation
quote: may challenge the person on the ground of party affiliation

claim: A candidate's party affiliation is set by the two most recent primaries they voted in, or by the county chair's certification
quote: The two (2) most recent primary elections in Indiana in which the candidate voted were primary elections held by the party with which the candidate claims affiliation.

claim: Parties nominate all candidates for the November municipal election in the municipal primary
quote: shall nominate all candidates to be voted for at the municipal election to be held in November

claim: County, township, city and town offices appear on the party primary ballot
quote: (B) Township trustee. (C) Township board member.

claim: Towns under 3,500 outside Marion County nominate major party candidates by convention unless the council adopts a primary by ordinance
quote: Unless a town legislative body adopts an ordinance under subsection (e), a town shall use the convention method described in this chapter to nominate major political party candidates for town offices.

claim: A candidate defeated in a primary or convention cannot run for the same office at the next general or municipal election
quote: is not eligible to become a candidate for the same office in the next general or municipal election

claim: The candidate with the most votes wins; there is no runoff
quote: the board shall declare the candidate receiving the highest number of votes for each office to be elected

claim: Independents and candidates of parties without primary access are nominated by petition
quote: represents a political party not qualified to nominate candidates in a primary or by convention

claim: Petition signers must be registered at their address and qualified to vote for the candidate
quote: A candidate may be nominated for an elected office by petition of voters who are:

claim: School board candidates are nominated only by petition
quote: A candidate for a school board office must file a petition of nomination

claim: A school board candidate states a party affiliation, independent, or no affiliation, and the statement is shown on the ballot
quote: the candidate's statement under this subdivision must be indicated on the ballot in the manner determined by the county election board

claim: A school board candidate may choose not to disclose any party affiliation
quote: That the candidate elects not to disclose any affiliation with a political party

claim: A straight-party vote does not count for any school board candidate
quote: a straight party vote does not count for any candidate for a school board office

claim: Elected school boards are chosen at the general election; some school corporations' plans do not provide for election
quote: If a plan provides for election of members of the governing body, the members of the governing body shall be elected at a general election.

claim: School board candidates with the most votes are elected
quote: The candidates who receive the most votes are elected.

claim: The three-member board of commissioners is the county executive
quote: The three (3) member board of commissioners of a county elected under this chapter is the county executive.

claim: Commissioners serve four-year staggered terms, one or two elected at each general election
quote: The number of members to be elected to the executive alternates between one (1) and two (2) at succeeding general elections.

claim: The seven-member county council is the county fiscal body
quote: The seven (7) member county council elected under this chapter is the county fiscal body.

claim: County council members serve four-year terms
quote: The term of office of a member of the fiscal body is four (4) years

claim: By default the council has four district members and three at-large members
quote: Three (3) at-large members of the fiscal body shall be elected by the voters of the whole county.

claim: A few large counties elect their council from single-member districts only, set by population bands in the statute
quote: shall divide the county into seven (7) single-member districts

claim: Counties elect a clerk of the circuit court, auditor, recorder, treasurer, sheriff, coroner and surveyor for four-year terms
quote: Clerk of the Circuit Court, Auditor, Recorder, Treasurer, Sheriff, Coroner, and Surveyor

claim: Clerk, auditor, recorder, treasurer, sheriff and coroner are limited to eight years in any twelve
quote: more than eight years in any period of twelve years

claim: The township trustee is the township executive, elected for four years
quote: The trustee is the township executive.

claim: Each township elects a three-member township board, five members in Marion County
quote: The township board in a county containing a consolidated city shall consist of five (5) members

claim: The township board is the township legislative body, with four-year terms
quote: The township board is the township legislative body.

claim: Only a few townships still elect a township assessor
quote: Township assessor (only in a township referred to in

claim: A 2026 law requires townships the state scores as designated to merge with another township in their county
quote: must merge with at least one (1) other township government in the county

claim: The township merger law does not apply in Marion County
quote: This chapter does not apply to a county having a consolidated city.

claim: All mergers under the 2026 law take effect by 1 January 2029
quote: All township government mergers under this chapter must be effective not later than January 1, 2029.

claim: Merged townships elect a three-member at-large board starting with the 2030 general election
quote: Beginning with the 2030 general election, all voters of the resulting merged township government shall elect a three (3) member township board.

claim: A municipality is a city or a town
quote: "Municipality" means city or town.

claim: Second class cities have 34,000 to 599,999 people; first class 600,000 or more
quote: Cities of 34,000 to 599,999 Second class cities

claim: A second class city keeps its class if its population falls below 34,000, unless it opts for third class
quote: remains a second class city even though its population decreases

claim: A third class city stays third class even after reaching 34,000 unless it opts up by ordinance
quote: a third class city remains a third class city even though the city attains a population of at least thirty-four thousand (34,000)

claim: The mayor is the city executive, elected for four years
quote: The term of office of a city executive is four (4) years

claim: Common council members serve four-year terms
quote: The term of office of a member of the legislative body is four (4) years, beginning at noon on January 1

claim: A second class city council has six district and three at-large members
quote: The legislative body is composed of six (6) members elected from the districts established under subsection (b) and three (3) at-large members.

claim: A third class city council has five district and two at-large members by default
quote: The legislative body is composed of five (5) members elected from the districts established under subsection (b) and two (2) at-large members.

claim: Second class cities elect a clerk, third class cities a clerk-treasurer
quote: by the voters of each third class city

claim: The town council is the legislative body and its president is the town executive; towns have no mayor
quote: The president of the town council selected under section 7 of this chapter is the town executive.

claim: Town council size may be set between three and seven by a vote of the town
quote: which must be at least three (3) and not more than seven (7)

claim: Town council members serve four-year terms by default
quote: the term of office of a member of the legislative body is four (4) years, beginning at noon January 1 after the member's election

claim: Towns elect a clerk-treasurer
quote: the clerk-treasurer elected under this chapter is both the town clerk and the town fiscal officer

claim: A town becomes a city only by a vote of its residents, and a town under 2,000 cannot
quote: A town with a population of less than two thousand (2,000) may not be changed into a city.

claim: Some third class cities use four district and three at-large members by ordinance
quote: The legislative body is composed of four (4) members elected from the districts established under subsection (j) and three (3) at-large members.

claim: County executives name the townships that will merge by 1 October 2027
quote: the county executive shall adopt a resolution that names the township governments that will merge

claim: The Indianapolis mayor is elected countywide in the municipal election
quote: shall be elected under IC 3-10-6 by the voters of the whole county

claim: The consolidated city of Indianapolis covers all of Marion County except the excluded cities
quote: all other territory in the county except territory of an excluded city

claim: The mayor is the executive of both the consolidated city and Marion County, elected countywide
quote: who is the executive of both the consolidated city and the county

claim: The city-county council is the legislative body of both, with 25 members
quote: The city-county council consists of twenty-five (25) members.

claim: All 25 city-county council members are elected from districts
quote: divide the whole county into twenty-five (25) districts

claim: In Marion County the treasurer, auditor and assessor serve ex officio as county commissioners
quote: These three (3) officers then serve ex officio as commissioners

claim: Until 2027 an excluded city is any municipality in the county over 5,000 people, other than the first class city
quote: having a population of more than five thousand (5,000) in the county is known as an excluded city

claim: From 1 January 2027 the excluded cities are named: Lawrence, Beech Grove, Southport, Speedway and Cumberland
quote: (1) The city of Lawrence. (2) The city of Beech Grove. (3) The city of Southport. (4) The town of Speedway. (5) The town of Cumberland.

claim: The first regular session convenes in November of even-numbered years to organize
quote: shall convene on the third Tuesday after the first Monday of November of each even-numbered year

claim: The General Assembly reconvenes no later than the fourth Monday in January
quote: shall reconvene in session no later than the fourth Monday in January of the following year

claim: The odd-year session must adjourn by 29 April
quote: shall adjourn sine die not later than April 29 in any odd-numbered year

claim: A one-day technical session in June of odd years can act on vetoed bills
quote: shall convene on the second Tuesday after the first Monday in June of each odd-numbered year

claim: The technical session considers bills vetoed by the governor
quote: Bills enacted during the first regular session vetoed by the governor.

claim: Special sessions last at most 30 session days or 40 calendar days
quote: shall continue for not more than thirty (30) session days nor more than forty (40) calendar days

claim: Sessions begin in January unless law sets another day
quote: unless a different day or place shall have been appointed by law

claim: The governor has seven days after presentment to act on a bill
quote: The Governor shall have seven days after the day of presentment to act upon such bill

claim: An unsigned, unvetoed bill becomes law on the eighth day after presentment
quote: eighth day after presentment

claim: Acts of a regular session take effect on 1 July unless the act says otherwise
quote: takes effect on July 1 next following its enactment, unless a different time is specified in the SECTION
